packs.title: Parks and Coast
packs.promise: Find new uses, playful forms and changing light across Antalya’s parks and coast.

q.s: Read a new use without losing sight of the old one.
st: From an open public path in Dokumapark, choose a stretch of former factory building. Find three present-day clues: an opening, a route and a place where people can pause.
For each clue, describe only what you can see. Then suggest how it helps someone use the park today; keep this interpretation separate from your observation.
Read the municipality’s short account of the site’s change from a cotton factory to a park with cultural uses. Mark that past use as documented, rather than something your three clues prove.
Choose one detail you would keep if this place changed again. Explain the practical job you would want it to continue doing.

q.s: Give two familiar play actions one new rule.
st: Choose two toys in a permitted display, or use the museum’s linked photographs. Name a possible play action for each, such as rolling, balancing, arranging or turning. A visible shape is a clue, not proof of how an old toy worked.
Combine those two actions into an invented toy. Sketch it or describe its parts using ordinary words; it does not need to be buildable.
Make a three-move play rule: a starting arrangement, one action and a way to finish. Test the rule mentally and change one part that is unclear.
Give your invention a short name. State which two observed features inspired it and which parts you made up.

q.s: Make a quiet pattern from the park around you.
st: Choose a comfortable public path or seat in the eastern part of Karaalioğlu Park. Pick four small sounds, or four visible changes if you prefer: leaves moving, footsteps, shade or light.
Give each observation a simple mark or word. Arrange them into a four-part score; use one mark twice so a motif returns.
Follow the score silently with your eyes, finger or imagined rhythm. Change the order once and decide which arrangement better conveys your pause in the park.
Write one sentence connecting your chosen order to an observation. No performance, audio recording or musical skill is needed.

packs.title: Kaleiçi Lanes
packs.promise: Turn Kaleiçi’s thresholds, layered buildings and harbour views into discoveries of your own.

q.s: Design a threshold from the way a lane filters light.
st: Follow a comfortable short part of Hesapçı Sokak. Collect three different ways an exterior edge filters light or a view: an overhang, shutter, tree, recessed doorway or another visible form.
For each, choose a job it could serve: reducing direct sun, leaving a view open or creating privacy. Make clear that this is your reading of a visible form, not a claim about the occupant.
Arrange two of your collected ideas around an imaginary doorway. Choose which belongs higher and which belongs nearer eye level, then explain the balance you want.
Check your design against the third idea. Would adding it help, or would it make the threshold too enclosed? Keep or omit it with a reason.

q.s: Let one observed setting start a story you clearly invent.
st: Choose a setting from the provincial museum photographs, the public exterior or a permitted museum display if visiting. Note two visible details that could shape an everyday scene.
Invent a fictional character with one simple task, such as finding a quiet seat or carrying a tray. Write two short scenes: before the task and after one small obstacle.
Use one observed detail in each scene. Change the character’s choice between the scenes rather than adding an unexplained historical event.
Label the setting details observed and your character, task and outcome invented.

q.s: Give a fixed edge and moving water different marks.
st: Choose a dry, open public viewpoint at the harbour. Pick one fixed edge, such as a quay or building line, and one changing line made by water, reflection or a gently moving moored boat.
Give the fixed edge a continuous mark and the changing line a broken or repeated mark. Place them together on a small page, or describe their positions in words.
Make a second version in which the changing line takes more space. Choose the version that better expresses what held your attention.
Add a short caption made only from observations. No boat name, historical claim or ticketed trip is needed.
